prose_changes.old: Across a single century a scattering of English men and women began writing about the inner life of prayer in their own language rather than in Latin — Richard Rolle the Yorkshire hermit with his Fire of Love, Walter Hilton with the Scale of Perfection, and the anonymous author of The Cloud of Unknowing, all writing for recluses and devout lay people rather than for scholars. Two of the voices are women's.
